nodes.name: Jeffrey Epstein
nodes.note: Financier. Pleaded guilty in Florida state court in 2008 (solicitation, including of a minor). Federal sex-trafficking charges July 2019; died in federal custody 10 Aug 2019, ruled suicide.

nodes.name: Ghislaine Maxwell
nodes.note: Convicted Dec 2021 on five counts including sex trafficking of a minor; 20-year sentence. Moved to FPC Bryan (minimum security) 1 Aug 2025 after two days of interviews with the Deputy AG.

nodes.name: Robert Maxwell
nodes.note: Publisher; Ghislaine Maxwell's father. Died at sea 1991 (ruled accidental; autopsies inconsistent). State funeral on the Mount of Olives. Documented ties are not transitive to the Epstein enterprise.

nodes.name: Les Wexner
nodes.note: L Brands founder. Gave Epstein full power of attorney (1991); $3.1B in stock sales overseen through 2006; later said Epstein misappropriated vast sums. No proceeding.

nodes.name: Leon Black
nodes.note: Apollo co-founder. Paid Epstein $158M (Apollo board review) plus $12M; about $170M by the Senate Finance count, for "tax advice". Denies misconduct.

nodes.name: Steven Hoffenberg
nodes.note: Towers Financial, a half-billion-dollar Ponzi scheme; served 20 years. Paid Epstein a $25,000-a-month consultancy and a $2M loan never repaid. Death 2022: verify record.

nodes.name: Southern Trust Company
nodes.note: Epstein's Virgin Islands firm. Ten-year EDC tax break; $391M in assets by 2018. The USVI AG later alleged it was a shell.

nodes.name: JPMorgan Chase
nodes.note: Epstein's bank 1998–2013, kept through his 2006 arrest and 2008 plea. $290M class settlement (June 2023) and $75M to the USVI. No admission.

nodes.name: Deutsche Bank
nodes.note: Took Epstein as a client in 2013 and kept him until 2018. $75M victims' settlement (2023); $150M NYDFS penalty (2020).

nodes.name: Bank of America
nodes.note: $72.5M settlement, approved by Judge Rakoff on 27 Aug 2026. No admission.

nodes.name: Jes Staley
nodes.note: Ran the JPMorgan relationship with Epstein. Banned by the UK FCA (2023, upheld on appeal). A civil allegation against him is unadjudicated.

nodes.name: Edmond de Rothschild group
nodes.note: Paris offices raided 20 Mar 2026 in a bribery probe into former employee Fabrice Aidan. CEO Ariane de Rothschild had documented contacts with Epstein. A reported $25M consulting fee is not yet verified.

nodes.name: Fabrice Aidan
nodes.note: French diplomat; worked at Edmond de Rothschild 2014–16. Alleged to have passed UN documents to Epstein; denies it. Under Paris probe.

nodes.name: Valar Ventures
nodes.note: Fintech fund co-founded by Peter Thiel. Epstein put in about $40M (2015–16), now worth about $170M and the estate's largest asset.

nodes.name: Carbyne (Reporty)
nodes.note: Israeli emergency-communications firm, chaired by Ehud Barak. Epstein invested through Barak's partnership.

nodes.name: Peter Thiel
nodes.note: PayPal, Palantir and Founders Fund co-founder. Solicited Epstein's investment on 15 Nov 2014. His spokesman confirms Epstein was a limited partner and denies co-ownership and any island visit.

nodes.name: Palantir
nodes.note: Data and defence contractor co-founded by Thiel. Hired Mandelson's firm Global Counsel as its UK lobbyist in 2018.

nodes.name: Elon Musk
nodes.note: 2012–13 emails about visiting the island (reported from the 2026 release), against his 2025 statement that he refused. Says he never went.

nodes.name: Bill Gates
nodes.note: Acknowledges meetings with Epstein (2011–14) and calls them a mistake. Epstein's 2013 self-sent drafts about him are Epstein's claims only; Gates denies them.

nodes.name: Reid Hoffman
nodes.note: LinkedIn co-founder. Epstein called him "a very close friend" (2014–15 emails). MIT fundraising link. The island visit is to be verified.

nodes.name: Brock Pierce
nodes.note: Tether co-founder. Correspondence with Epstein; reported route for Epstein's Coinbase stake. To verify.

nodes.name: Boris Nikolic
nodes.note: Former science adviser to Bill Gates. Introduced Epstein to people by email (2011). To verify.

nodes.name: Larry Ellison
nodes.note: In the contact book with three numbers and in 23 case documents. No flight logs, no emails, no allegations: the thinnest edge on the map.

nodes.name: Donald Trump
nodes.note: Social friendship from about 1987 to 2004 (photos, 2002 quote); says he banned Epstein from Mar-a-Lago. Named over 1,000 times in the files. No accuser has alleged conduct in a proceeding that produced a finding.

nodes.name: Bill Clinton
nodes.note: Flights in the early 2000s (manifests). Denies knowledge of the crimes. Deposed by House Oversight on 27 Feb 2026.

nodes.name: Hillary Clinton
nodes.note: Deposed by House Oversight on 26 Feb 2026. Spouse of Bill Clinton. Her record is kept separate from his (family guardrail).

nodes.name: Peter Mandelson
nodes.note: Former UK cabinet minister and US ambassador. Friendship 2002–2011; the files show him passing government information. Arrested 24 Feb 2026 (misconduct in public office); bailed.

nodes.name: Global Counsel
nodes.note: Lobbying firm co-founded by Mandelson (2010). He kept a stake of about 21%. Palantir's UK lobbyist from 2018.

nodes.name: Ehud Barak
nodes.note: Former Israeli PM and defence minister. Post-2008 visits and business with Epstein; Côte d'Ivoire surveillance brokering 2012–14. A separate published allegation, which he denies, is kept apart from the business record.

nodes.name: State of Israel (government)
nodes.note: A node for documented state acts only: offices held, a state funeral, a government agency. Never a stand-in for a people or a faith.

nodes.name: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor
nodes.note: Friendship with Epstein; Giuffre's sworn allegation; civil suit settled 2022 without admission. Titles removed Oct 2025. Arrested 19 Feb 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office.

nodes.name: Sarah Ferguson
nodes.note: Andrew's former wife. 2011 correspondence with Epstein reported from the release. To verify.

nodes.name: Larry Summers
nodes.note: Former Treasury Secretary and Harvard president. Correspondence with Epstein after 2008. Stepped back from roles in 2025 (to verify).

nodes.name: Kathryn Ruemmler
nodes.note: Former Obama White House counsel; later Goldman Sachs chief legal officer. Correspondence and gifts reported from the release. To verify.

nodes.name: Howard Lutnick
nodes.note: US Commerce Secretary. Former neighbour. Has acknowledged a 2012 family lunch on the island. AdFin co-investment and later emails reported; his 2005 cut-off account conflicts with the files. To verify.

nodes.name: Steve Bannon
nodes.note: Recorded a long on-camera interview with Epstein; strategy texts 2017–19 reported. To verify.

nodes.name: Bill Richardson
nodes.note: Former New Mexico governor (d. 2023). Named in Giuffre's sworn deposition; denied it.

nodes.name: Crown Princess Mette-Marit
nodes.note: Norway. Emails 2011–14 and a 2013 stay reported from the release; has apologised. To verify.

nodes.name: Thorbjørn Jagland
nodes.note: Former Norwegian PM. Reported corruption probe over gifts/loans. To verify.

nodes.name: Sultan bin Sulayem
nodes.note: DP World chairman. Correspondence reported from the release, and a reported role in a Great St. James purchase vehicle. To verify; get DP World's response.

nodes.name: Woody Allen
nodes.note: Frequent social contact in the 2010s reported from the release; reported offer to edit the Bannon footage. To verify.

nodes.name: Noam Chomsky
nodes.note: Met Epstein after 2008 (acknowledged). A 2019 advice email is reported. To verify.

nodes.name: Richard Branson
nodes.note: 2013 email and PR suggestions reported; Virgin says the meeting was business and the women were adults. To verify.

nodes.name: Jean-Luc Brunel
nodes.note: Model agent (MC2). Charged in France (rape of minors); found dead in his Paris cell in 2022 before trial.

nodes.name: Harvard University
nodes.note: Took Epstein money before the conviction.

nodes.name: MIT Media Lab
nodes.note: MIT's own review: nine of ten gifts came after the 2008 conviction.

nodes.name: US Department of Justice
nodes.note: Controls charging and release. The 2008 agreement, the July 2025 "no client list" memo, the 2026 release and redactions.

nodes.name: FBI
nodes.note: Logged Maria Farmer's 1996 complaint and opened no case until 2006. Searched the safe in 2019. Ran the 2025 file review.

nodes.name: 2008 Non-Prosecution Agreement
nodes.note: Signed 24 Sept 2007. Immunised Epstein, four named people and unnamed "potential co-conspirators". Concealed from victims; ruled to violate the CVRA in 2019.

nodes.name: Alexander Acosta
nodes.note: US Attorney (SD Fla.) who approved the 2008 agreement. Later Labor Secretary; resigned July 2019. OPR (2020): "poor judgment".

nodes.name: Marie Villafaña
nodes.note: Lead federal prosecutor. Prepared the prosecution memo and the draft indictment (2007); the defence pushed for her removal. To verify the page counts.

nodes.name: Judge Kenneth Marra
nodes.note: Ruled in Feb 2019 that the government broke the law (CVRA) by concealing the agreement from victims.

nodes.name: Alan Dershowitz
nodes.note: Epstein's defence lawyer in 2007–08. Giuffre's allegation against him was withdrawn in the 2022 settlement: the book's case for caution.

nodes.name: Pam Bondi
nodes.note: Attorney General 2025–Apr 2026: "client list on my desk" (Feb 2025); July 2025 memo; Feb 2026 hearing; subpoenaed Mar 2026; fired Apr 2026.

nodes.name: Todd Blanche
nodes.note: Trump's former defence lawyer; Deputy AG, later acting AG. Interviewed Maxwell for two days in July 2025. Committed to Congress on 19 May 2026 not to recommend her pardon. Defendant in Phang v. Blanche.

nodes.name: Kash Patel
nodes.note: FBI Director during the 2025 review and the July 2025 memo.

nodes.name: Epstein Files Transparency Act
nodes.note: H.R. 4405: introduced 15 July 2025, passed 427–1, signed 19 Nov 2025. ~3.5M pages released 30 Jan 2026 of ~6M identified. EFTA II (H.R. 9694) introduced July 2026.

nodes.name: Thomas Massie
nodes.note: Filed the discharge petition (Sept 2025) that forced the vote.

nodes.name: Ro Khanna
nodes.note: Introduced the Act on 15 July 2025.

nodes.name: Speaker Mike Johnson
nodes.note: Sent the House home early in July 2025 ahead of Epstein votes (reported). To verify.

nodes.name: House Oversight Committee
nodes.note: Estate photo releases (Dec 2025); Clinton depositions (Feb 2026); Bondi subpoena (Mar 2026).

nodes.name: Phang v. Blanche
nodes.note: Journalist Katie Phang's suit under the Act. Judge Sullivan's June 2026 injunction ordered a foreign-language review; the D.C. Circuit refused to pause it on 28 Oct 2026.

nodes.name: FBI source report EFTA00090314
nodes.note: Oct 2020 confidential-source report in the release. Claims Epstein was "trained" under Barak and tied to Mossad. Raw, unverified source reporting; quoted as such and never as a finding.

nodes.name: CIA
nodes.note: The second-hand report that Acosta said Epstein "belonged to intelligence" names no agency and was never confirmed.

nodes.name: NSA
nodes.note: Bulk domestic call-record collection through Epstein's active years; raw SIGINT shared with Unit 8200 under a memorandum (Snowden, 2013).

nodes.name: Unit 8200
nodes.note: Israeli SIGINT unit; received raw NSA data under the memorandum.

nodes.name: Maria Farmer
nodes.note: Reported Epstein and Maxwell to the FBI on 29 Aug 1996.

nodes.name: Virginia Giuffre
nodes.note: Survivor and plaintiff. Sued Maxwell (2015) and Andrew (settled 2022). Died April 2025; ruled suicide per family and police reports.

nodes.name: Vicky Ward
nodes.note: Vanity Fair 2002–03 profile; the Farmer sisters' allegations were cut after Epstein visited the editor.

nodes.name: 9 East 71st Street
nodes.note: Townhouse, about 21,000 sq ft. Bought by Wexner in 1989 and transferred to an Epstein entity. Sold 2021.

nodes.name: El Brillo Way, Palm Beach
nodes.note: Site of the 2005 police investigation (more than 30 underage victims identified).

nodes.name: Little St. James
nodes.note: Bought 1998. Sold in 2023 with Great St. James for $60M to Stephen Deckoff for a resort.

nodes.name: Great St. James
nodes.note: Bought about 2016 (reportedly via a holding company). Sold in 2023 with Little St. James.

nodes.name: Zorro Ranch, New Mexico
nodes.note: About 7,500 acres, bought 1993. State case closed 2019 at federal request; reopened Feb 2026; searched Mar 2026; legislature formed a truth commission. Sold 2023 to the Huffines family.

nodes.name: Paris apartment
nodes.note: Avenue Foch. Listed in the estate at $8.7M.

nodes.name: New Mexico Attorney General
nodes.note: Raúl Torrez reopened the Zorro Ranch investigation (Feb 2026).

nodes.name: US Virgin Islands government
nodes.note: Granted the Southern Trust tax break; later sued JPMorgan ($75M).

nodes.name: UK police
nodes.note: Arrested Andrew (19 Feb 2026) and Mandelson (24 Feb 2026) on suspicion of misconduct in public office.

nodes.name: Paris prosecutor
nodes.note: Two Epstein-linked probes opened 18 Feb 2026 (trafficking; laundering, corruption and tax fraud). About 20 suspected victims heard by May 2026.

nodes.name: Simon Andriesz
nodes.note: Former BGC managing director; CFTC whistleblower (about $420k). Took claims about Lutnick and Epstein to the FBI (2020–21) and to House Oversight (2026). Died in Thailand, late Sept 2026, aged 57. No official cause published; family says suicide, no foul play. The FCA is reviewing its own handling.

nodes.name: Daniel Siad
nodes.note: Model scout. Brunel forwarded his terms to Epstein in 2010 (per the files; to pull). Rape complaint filed Feb 2026 (denied). Never questioned. Died 20 Jul 2026; natural cardiac death; case closed 22 Oct 2026.

nodes.name: Tova Noel
nodes.note: MCC guard on duty on 9–10 Aug 2019. Charged with falsifying records (dropped); fired. Searched for Epstein news about 40 minutes before he was found; $5,000 cash deposit ten days before. Told House Oversight (18 May 2026) the money was her savings and that she believes it was suicide.

nodes.name: Efrain Reyes
nodes.note: Epstein's last cellmate; moved out the morning before and not replaced. Told the NYT he warned guards. Died Nov 2020 (COVID, per police).

nodes.name: Arthur Shapiro
nodes.note: Columbus lawyer whose firm worked for The Limited. Shot dead 6 Mar 1985, the day before a grand-jury appearance; unsolved. A 1991 police report was ordered destroyed by the chief. Link to Epstein runs through Wexner only.

nodes.name: Mark Middleton
nodes.note: Clinton White House aide; reported as signing Epstein in on White House visits (to verify). Died 7 May 2022, Arkansas; ruled suicide; the sheriff's reports were inconsistent about the weapon.

nodes.name: MCC New York (BOP)
nodes.note: Where Epstein died. IG (2023): significant misconduct (suicide watch lifted, no cellmate, rounds not done, records falsified, cameras broken). No evidence of criminality found.

nodes.name: Michael Freeman
nodes.note: Forensic medicine professor; editor of the Journal of Forensic and Legal Medicine. Reviewed the medical examiner's file (given by Mark Epstein). UCL lecture 16 Nov 2026.

nodes.name: UK Financial Conduct Authority
nodes.note: Appointed Lea Paterson to review its handling of Andriesz's whistleblowing (Oct 2026).

nodes.name: Sarah Kellen
nodes.note: Assistant about 2001–13: scheduling; "given a directory of names and told whom to call" (DOJ memo, Dec 2019). Named in the 2008 NPA; never charged; DOJ did not dispute she was also a victim. Not interviewed by law enforcement until after the July 2019 arrest. House Oversight interview 21 May 2026.

nodes.name: Lesley Groff
nodes.note: Executive assistant 2001–Jul 2019; managed the schedule. Named in the 2008 NPA; never charged; civil suits dismissed. Interviewed by prosecutors 2021; House Oversight 9 Jun 2026 (says she was unaware). Survivors dispute her account.

nodes.name: Adriana Ross
nodes.note: Assistant; named in the 2008 NPA; on flight logs. Never charged. No public interview record found.

nodes.name: Nadia Marcinko
nodes.note: Named in the 2008 NPA; on flight logs. Never charged. No public interview record found.

nodes.name: Juan Alessi
nodes.note: Palm Beach house manager (1990s–2002). Deposed 2009; witness at the Maxwell trial (2021). Not charged.

nodes.name: Alfredo Rodriguez
nodes.note: Palm Beach butler (2004–05). Kept the contact book "as insurance". Convicted 2010 for trying to sell it to an undercover FBI agent. Died about 2015.

nodes.name: Larry Visoski
nodes.note: Chief pilot. Witness at the Maxwell trial (2021). Not charged.

nodes.name: David Rodgers
nodes.note: Pilot; kept flight logs. Deposed; in DOJ trial prep (2021). Not charged.

nodes.name: Darren Indyke
nodes.note: Epstein's lawyer; estate co-executor. A 2024 class action alleged he helped structure cash access and sham marriages (denied). Estate settled for $25–35M (Feb 2026), no admission.

nodes.name: Richard Kahn
nodes.note: Epstein's accountant; estate co-executor. Same 2024 class action (denied); same settlement.

nodes.name: Melania Trump
nodes.note: Photographed with Trump, Epstein and Maxwell at Mar-a-Lago (Feb 2000). Maxwell emails in the files ("casual", she says). Denied any friendship and denied that Epstein introduced her to Trump (Apr 2026, unsworn). Her record is kept separate from her husband's.

nodes.name: Philip Levine
nodes.note: Former Miami Beach mayor. Named by Kellen to House Oversight (May 2026) in an assault allegation; his spokesperson says it was a consensual encounter. Unadjudicated; referred to DOJ by Comer (Jun 2026).

nodes.name: Frédéric Fekkai
nodes.note: Hairstylist. Named by Kellen to House Oversight (May 2026) in an assault allegation; denies abusing anyone. Unadjudicated; referred to DOJ (Jun 2026).

nodes.name: DEA / OCDETF
nodes.note: Operation "Chain Reaction" (NY-NYS-0829): a May 2015 memo names Epstein plus 14 redacted targets for wire transfers tied to drugs and/or prostitution in the USVI and NYC. No one charged; how it ended is not on the record. Sen. Wyden asked six questions (Feb 2026).

nodes.name: Roy Black
nodes.note: Epstein's criminal defence lawyer (2005–08). Per an Oct 2005 memo in the files, items were removed from the Palm Beach house "pursuant to the instructions" of Black.

nodes.name: William Riley
nodes.note: Private investigator for Epstein; received the removed Palm Beach items "for inventory and safekeeping"; managed storage units (paid until at least 2010). Contested a 2007 subpoena. Rep. Garcia demanded the drives (Mar 2026).

nodes.name: Paul Lavery
nodes.note: Private investigator who removed about 100 items, including 3 computers, from the Palm Beach house in Oct 2005, less than two weeks before the police search (Oct 2005 memo).

nodes.name: Merwin Dela Cruz
nodes.note: NYC house manager. Packed the unseized safe contents into suitcases after the July 2019 search and left them with Kahn's doorman; returned about 5 days later.

nodes.name: Palm Beach computers and items (2005)
nodes.note: 3 computers, 29 phone directories, a masseuse list, nude photos, over 40 VHS tapes, cash. Removed before the police search; in storage until at least 2010; location now unknown. Prosecutors appear never to have accessed them.

nodes.name: FBI evidence index (2007/2019 searches)
nodes.note: 40 computers and devices, 26 drives, over 70 CDs, 6 recording devices, the island logbook, a "document with names", employee lists, and 3 discs of Maxwell phone intercepts. Over 300 GB (DOJ). In FBI custody.

nodes.name: MCC master video (FBI item 1B60)
nodes.note: Master recording of the jail video archives. Destruction authorised June 2024 as "no longer pertinent". Re-recorded May 2025 with a 62-second gap.

nodes.name: NM Survivors' Truth Commission
nodes.note: Created by House Resolution 1 (62–0, Feb 2026). Initial report 5 Aug 2026: at least 5 victims at the ranch (1996–2012), 227 flights; no search until Mar 2026. 20 subpoenas; SDNY, the FAA and JPMorgan refused or did not respond. Final report due 31 Dec 2026.

nodes.name: US Attorney, SDNY
nodes.note: Brought the 2019 case and Maxwell's prosecution. Asked New Mexico to close its 2019 case. Refused or did not respond to the NM commission's subpoena (2026).

nodes.name: Maple Inc.
nodes.note: USVI shell holding the Manhattan townhouse (recorded transfer from Wexner 2011).

nodes.name: Nautilus Inc.
nodes.note: Shell holding Little St. James.

nodes.name: Great St. Jim LLC
nodes.note: Shell holding Great St. James (bought 2016, $22.5M).

nodes.name: Cypress Inc.
nodes.note: USVI shell holding Zorro Ranch.

nodes.name: LSJE LLC
nodes.note: Shell that paid island employees.

nodes.name: Financial Trust Co.
nodes.note: Epstein's money-management firm (NY 1981, later USVI).

nodes.name: 301 East 66th Street apartments
nodes.note: Owned via a company linked to Mark Epstein; effectively controlled by Epstein (Drop Site). Barak's stays 2016–17.

nodes.name: NJ security contractor (2008)
nodes.note: Proposed and installed a camera-system upgrade at the townhouse, Nov 2008 – Mar 2009 (~$43k approved; $53,190 invoiced). Records show no blackmail or recording purpose (fact-check).

nodes.name: The Spy Store, Fort Lauderdale
nodes.note: Feb 2014: motion-sensor hidden cameras bought by pilot Visoski at Epstein's request for Palm Beach.

nodes.name: Ubiquiti (equipment)
nodes.note: UniFi Wi-Fi, a G3 camera and a video recorder on Little St. James (2017–19), via an Amazon order and a UPS shipment; recorder seized by the FBI. No evidence the company knew of the use.

nodes.name: Liston Thomas
nodes.note: Tech contractor who scheduled the island equipment installation (Mar 2019).

nodes.name: Israel's Permanent Mission to the UN
nodes.note: Protective services (Rafi Shlomo) installed and maintained alarms and sensors at the 66th Street apartment for Barak's stays, 2016–17; background checks on Epstein staff. Protective security; not evidence that Epstein worked for Israel.

nodes.name: MC2 Model Management
nodes.note: Brunel's agency; funded by Epstein (Guardian). The modelling recruitment route.
